publicationDecision.authorisation: Matt's standing Medicines Watch instruction authorises needed evidence-backed informational additions and corrections to go live without repeat permission.
publicationDecision.scope: Add seven previously untracked sponsor-submitted ribupatide and HRS-4729 records and one primary sponsor results announcement to the existing programme entries. Editorial authorisation is not clinical approval.

reviewType: AI-assisted primary-source factual review; not clinical approval

fields.stage: Global Phase 3 fully enrolled; China specialist-indication studies active
fields.summaryToAppend: Broader registry discovery found two recruiting Chinese Phase 3 obstructive-sleep-apnoea studies (NCT06974851 and PAP-treated NCT06994650), a recruiting 9,262-participant Phase 3 cardiovascular-outcomes study (NCT07551492), and an active-not-recruiting 48-participant Phase 1 adolescent-obesity study (NCT07559136). NCT07660848 separately studies ribupatide and HRS-4729 arms in recruiting Phase 2 MASH research. Hengrui also reported topline results from the 158-participant Phase 2 HRS9531-207 study in women with obesity and polycystic ovary syndrome (NCT06595797); the older registry record remains UNKNOWN, retains 144 estimated participants and has no posted results.
fields.limitationsToAppend: These are China-based indication-specific studies, not evidence that sleep apnoea, cardiovascular disease, adolescent obesity, MASH or polycystic ovary syndrome are authorised ribupatide indications. Recruiting and active-not-recruiting records have no posted results. The 9,262-participant cardiovascular study is event-driven and its estimated 2031 completion is not a completed outcome. Hengrui's polycystic-ovary-syndrome findings are sponsor-reported topline results; the registry discrepancy and absence of registry-posted results remain explicit. None establishes UK authorisation, NICE/NHS access, UK supply or clinical approval.

configuredSourcePass.boundary: The SELECT-only response verifies configured-source monitoring only. It does not renew factual reviews, approve changed wording or prove complete industry coverage. The unchanged Zealand 403 remains explicit.

discoveryPass.method: A separate broad and undated programme, formulation, specialist-indication and international registry pass was reconciled with current main, dated receipts and open Watch PRs after the configured-source pass.
discoveryPass.included: Seven distinct sponsor-submitted records update the existing ribupatide injection, oral ribupatide and KAI-4729 entries. The Hengrui announcement resolves drug identity and records sponsor-reported PCOS/PMOS topline evidence while the older conflicting registry remains visible.
discoveryPass.notDuplicated: The records extend existing programmes and do not inflate the 97-programme catalogue. PR 851 is merged and no open Medicines Watch review PR was present.
incompleteChecks: Search indexing can lag; selected developers, domains and registry queries cannot exclude unannounced programmes, older omissions or other international developers.
The PCOS/PMOS terminology differs between the sponsor announcement and registry, and the sponsor's 158 participants conflicts with the registry's older 144 estimate. Both dated accounts are retained.
No new MHRA authorisation, NICE recommendation, NHS access decision or verified UK supply change was established.

failedChecks.impact: The prior source remains verification pending; successful new source reviews do not replace or green that blocked baseline.

nextAction: Run the full Watch and release gates, publish the exact passing head through the guarded workflow, verify the live ribupatide entries, Treatments link and SELECT-only health endpoint, and retain the Zealand 403 until a complete primary response can be captured.
